html:
SMTO-LLM-0094 — The computer running your model ran out of memory

GUID: 8192110e-3bd2-42dd-baf5-fbc2270ba8a7
Slug: provider-memory-exhausted
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • The model service said it didn't have enough memory to handle SMTO's request, so no answer came back. This happens on the computer that runs the model, not in SMTO.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If other people or programs are using the same model service right now, wait until their work finishes. Requests running at the same time share the model's memory, so fewer requests can leave room for yours.
  2. Ask the person who runs the model service to check its memory use and logs, and adjust it so it fits the computer, for example a smaller model or fewer requests at once. Only they can see the model computer's memory and change how the model is loaded.
  3. When they say it has recovered, open Settings › Setup › Model routing and select Check saved model on that model's card. One small test request shows the service can answer again before you restart larger work.
  4. Before asking SMTO to continue a task that stopped with this error, open its Conversation and check which steps it already finished. Steps finished before the error may already have made changes, and repeating them could do them twice.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes, and new requests get answers without a memory error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model service. Restarting SMTO won't help; the memory shortage is on the computer that runs the model.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model service returned a server error with an explicit out_of_memory or cuda_out_of_memory error code.

What this means

  • The serving process reported insufficient memory. Available accelerator memory, model size and concurrent requests can contribute; SMTO cannot inspect remote hardware from this response.

Why this can happen

  • The serving process reported insufficient memory. Available accelerator memory, model size and concurrent requests can contribute; SMTO cannot inspect remote hardware from this response.

How to diagnose it

  • The provider returned an explicit out-of-memory error code.
  • The service completes a model request without reporting memory exhaustion.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the provider's serving logs and GPU/host memory at the failure time, then reduce concurrent requests, the served context length or the model size (for vLLM, for example --max-model-len or --gpu-memory-utilization) so the deployment fits. Re-run Check saved model once the service recovers, and inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.
  • Provider administrator: inspect serving logs and memory usage. Reduce confirmed concurrency pressure or adjust the deployment to fit available resources; submit work again after the service recovers.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • The service completes a model request without reporting memory exhaustion.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
